messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Errors in temporal thinning, Two problems occoured
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Errors in temporal thinning, Two problems occoured
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ilona,

first, computation time: I believe the problem with manually running assessTemporalIndependence is that the amount of time it takes increases exponentially with the number of records. Normally it is called for each station individually, and then it doesn't take long (when running recordTable, assessTemporalIndependence  is called for every station). You can do the same by splitting your record table by stations (or station and camera, whichever is appropriate) with something like:
records_split <- split(records_filter_KOOM, f = list(records_filter_KOOM$Camera.Trap.name <http://Camera.Trap.name>, records_filter_KOOM$Camera.Serial.Number))

records_split_independent <- lapply(records_split, FUN = camtrapR:::assessTemporalIndependence,
                                    deltaTimeComparedTo = "lastIndependentRecord",
                                    ...)    # add the other arguments

out <- do.call("rbind", records_split_independent)   # reassemble

Regarding one species only, I don't know why that would happen. How many species are there in
records_filter_TUM before running  assessTemporalIndependence? Feel free to email me the table and I'll try it myself. What confuses me though is that you first work on records_filter_TUM, then call assessTemporalIndependence(records_filter_SOJO.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] timeShiftImages works for videos?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Raquel,

currently timeShiftImages only works with jpg files. I never tried it with videos though and I'm not sure how well it will work. The issue is that there are many different video file formats and no proper standard regarding the date/time field in the metadata.

I believe the best solution for you at the moment would be to just run recordTable like normal (extracting the wrong dates), and then edit the dates of the output. The lubridate package is very powerful for that purpose, and allows different types of time differences to be calculated.

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Re: [camtrapR] Problem with the output of detectionHistory
messages.subject_clean: [camtrapR] Problem with the output of detectionHistory
messages.body_plain:
Hi Maca,

this is expected behaviour. Please see Vignette 3, under "Handling of incomplete occasions".

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/camtrapR/vignettes/camtrapr3.html#Occupancy_analyses

One of the reasons for NA instead of 0 in detection histories is that 0 is considered a non-detection, which assumes there was a chance of detecting the species. With practical terms, with effort = 0, there is 0 chance of detecting a species. But, in terms of the model, even with effort = 0, the detection probabilities at those occasions are > 0, because the probabilities in the occupancy models can't be 0 or 1 due to the logit transformation.

So, the danger with 0 detection histories when there was 0 effort is that the model would assume that there was a small chance of detecting the species, when in reality it was 0. Therefore, using NA instead of 0 prevents the models from using cells with no effort, and thus ensures the probabilities are estimates correctly (using only cells for which there was at least some effort).

In mathematical terms, say you use effort as a covariate on detection probability, The logit of the detection probability is:

logit(p) = beta_0 + beta_1 * effort

beta_0 is the intercept, beta_1 is the effect of effort (in days). With effort = 0 (cameras not operating), we get:

logit(p) = beta_0

No matter how small we choose beta_0 (or rather, how small the model estimates it to be), the resulting detection probability at effort = 0 will not be 0 due to the logit transformation, thus allowing for detections when they were impossible.

I believe that was the main reasoning behind this admittedly confusing design choice. Does that answer your question?

Best regards,

Jürgen

messages.subject: Issue with recordTable() reading video files
messages.subject_clean: Issue with recordTable() reading video files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Juergen,

I am in the process of using a small sample of video files to learn camtrapR and get the workflow figured out before using it for a large dataset. I am using Digikam and have the database file located in within a 'session' folder containing the station subdirectories (attached).

I ran into some issues with recordTable(), where I received the following error message for station folders that contain videos,

Warning:  090.1.2:   metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'.

I have been troubleshooting this problem with Joel Ruprecht, who has experience with using video files in camtrapR, and here's what we've figured out.

-If a photo (jpg file) is copied into any of the station folders, recordTable() is able to read it correctly with all of it associated tags, although it cannot read the video files. This is when I have InDir set to the same file path as the attached snip, 'digikam_db_location(2)'.

-If InDir is changed to a particular station folder (e.g. ".../W20/069.7.1"), recordTable() can read all of those video files correctly along with all of their associated tags.

-Using the source code (attached) confirmed that the tag info is being correctly read from the database.

Any ideas as to whether or not this is an issue on my end? Also, I realize that before I include data from a new session, I will need to move the digikam database files to the folder containing the different sessions (e.g. W20, W21, etc.). Not sure how relevant that is, but I wanted to clarify that my database files and video files will have to be separated by several folders.

Thanks very much for the help with this!

Wes

messages.body_plain:
Hi Juergen,

I just wanted to provide a few details about my experience having similar issues with a different dataset. When I called recordTable() to extract tags from videos with inDir set to the folder containing all the stations, it worked perfectly for 25 out of 28 stations. But for 3 stations, I got the same warning message "metadataSpeciesTag 'Species' not found in image metadata tag 'HierarchicalSubject'" even though those 3 stations had 'Species' video tags. When I then pointed inDir to the station folder for each of those 3 stations, it extracted the video tags fine. I can find no pattern to the 3 problematic stations (e.g. it happened on 2 camera types, Browning and Bushnell, and two file types, mp4 and avi).

For me it wasn't a big deal, I just ran recordTable() on the 3 stations separately and used rbind() to combine them. So although my issue is resolved, I just wanted to provide these details in case it helps with troubleshooting for others with larger datasets.

Thanks for all your work on this fine package!

Joel
